answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 4 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the karst hash is stored at intake, the mesa graph groups the endorsements and the mirror audit shows the collapse. An operator copying one text across 24 aliases hence pays for 24 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
